newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: JSC loss due to corrugated container prices.
newsitem.headline: JSC loss due to corrugated container prices.

text.p: Jefferson Smurfit Corporation said on Thursday that a net loss of $4 million in the second quarter was primarily due to corrugated container prices which were on average significantly below last year's levels.

But JSC, a 46.5 percent owned associate of Irish paper manufacturer Jefferson Smurfit Group Plc, said it should benefit in the second half from an improving market climate, strong volume and higher product prices, offset in part by higher fibre costs.
The company said that despite the loss, its second quarter performance reflected several positives.

"First of all, the loss was less than expected, partly as a result of the contribution of our non-container business," Richard W. Graham, JSC's president and chief executive officer said in a statement.
He said folding carton shipments increased significantly over year-ago quarter levels while demand for coated recycled boxboard on the open market was strong.
"Our newsprint business posted better-than-expected profits as a result of the successful implementation of a newsprint price increase," Graham said.
Corrugated container shipments also increased substantially compared to the second quarter of 1996 and the increased volume contributed to the better-than-expected result, he said.
Graham also said market trends were favourable with demand for packaging healthy across its customer base while prices began to stabilise.

"Recovered fibre prices were firm to improving for most grades, reflecting healthy global demand. Inventories declined through the quarter. As a result of these trends, we have announced paperboard and packaging prices increases to take effect from the third quarter."
